macOS: allow install_name_tool -id to work

This is required so that LC_ID_DYLIB may be set using install_name_tool
by downstream consumers. What the LC_ID_DYLIB field does is that when
the dylib is given to the linker, it forms the path the dylib in
question will be referred to in the RPATH of the resulting dependent
dylibs/executables.

This is necessary to support nixpkgs which wants to set this field to
/nix/store/..., but hits an error if we try doing that due to lack of
padding in the executable header (requiring relinking upstream, which,
hi!).

```
       > /nix/store/9n1n53pyrjdanm5gsxcgchr9v0i0401v-pdfium-lib/lib/libpdfium.dylib: fixing dylib
       > error: install_name_tool: changing install names or rpaths can't be redone for: /nix/store/9n1n53pyrjdanm5gsxcgchr9v0i0401v-p
dfium-lib/lib/libpdfium.dylib (for architecture arm64) because larger updated load commands do not fit (the program must be relinked, 
and you may need to use -headerpad or -headerpad_max_install_names)
```

iOS: set `ios_deployment_target` to `17.0` (`17.4` when V8 is enabled)

Without this setting, the build inherits Chromium's default from
build/config/ios/ios_sdk_overrides.gni, which is 26.0 when use_blink is true.
That default has moved twice with no change in this repo — 17.4 to 18.4 at
chromium/7202, 18.4 to 26.0 at chromium/7337 — so the published floor has been
tracking Chromium rather than anything about pdfium.

V8 builds hard-link BrowserEngineKit, which is iOS 17.4+, so the two
configurations do not share a floor: a V8 build declaring 17.0 compiles cleanly
and then fails in dyld at load time on anything below 17.4.

Tag static artifacts with a -static suffix, and build static packages

Use the system libc++ for static Apple builds

A static libpdfium.a is linked into the consumer's binary, which uses the
platform libc++. Chromium's bundled libc++ mangles as std::__Cr and the
archive does not carry its compiled iostream objects, so 'build.sh -s ios'
produces an archive that fails to link with undefined std::__Cr::ios_base
symbols once pdfium's FDF code is pulled in.

Set use_custom_libcxx=false for static mac/ios builds, matching what is
already done for static linux-arm64, android, emscripten and musl.

Link the Apple system frameworks a static pdfium needs

A shared build resolves CoreFoundation and CoreGraphics itself; a static
archive leaves them to the consumer, so the example in steps/09-test.sh
fails to link against a static Apple build with undefined _CFRelease,
_CGBitmapContextCreate and similar.

Use the platform C++ library for every static build

Chromium's bundled libc++ is never a dependency of a static_library target,
so its objects are missing from libpdfium.a on every platform, not just Apple.
